thread:
maya (Support): FYI customer reported tool-calling mixup when we fan out two tools in parallel. tool_result from toolA sometimes shows up attached to toolB's call_id. Correlation ID: cid_07f4e9. Customer impact: wrong tool outputs in final payload.
lee (eng-oncall): Ugh, can you paste the exact request payload + headers?
maya (Support): Here's the simplified request we sent (redacted):
```json
{
  "request_id": "cid_07f4e9",
  "model": "rw/2026-base",
  "input": "Summarize and lookup prices",
  "tools": [
    {"name": "price_lookup", "args": {"sku": "SKU-123"}},
    {"name": "summarizer", "args": {"text": "<...>"}}
  ],
  "parallel_tools": true
}
```
maya (Support): curl they used for repro:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'x-rw-correlation: cid_07f4e9' \n  -d @payload.json
```
maya (Support): Customer attachments show response where `tool_result` with `price_lookup` output has `tool_call_id` of the summarizer call. They see price text inserted into summary field.
lee (eng-oncall): Does the customer see any schema validation errors?
maya (Support): No validation errors. Everything returns 200. It's only the mapping of tool_result->tool metadata that's wrong.
zack (eng-runtime): This smells like a race in the fanout path where we merge results by timestamp instead of stable tool_call_id. Can you check the response envelope? Do we include both `tool_name` and `tool_call_id` in each tool_result?
maya (Support): We only see `tool_name` and `tool_call_id` in some responses. Sometimes `tool_call_id` is missing (null). Example snippet from customer:
```json
{
  "tool_results": [
    {"tool_name":"summarizer","tool_call_id": null, "output":"Prices: $19"},
    {"tool_name":"price_lookup","tool_call_id":"tc_8b2f", "output":"(ok) summarized text"}
  ]
}
```
alice (QA): I tried to reproduce in staging with high-concurrency and turned on `x-rw-debug: tool-trace`. I can repro intermittently. When it happens, logs show two worker threads writing the `tool_results` array concurrently; the merge uses array index instead of the original call token.
lee (eng-oncall): Can you paste the debug log lines around the merge?
alice (QA): Relevant lines:
```
2026-03-05T12:11:02.012Z [worker-3] tool_call(tc_8b2f) finished -> enqueued result idx=1
2026-03-05T12:11:02.013Z [worker-5] tool_call(tc_8b2a) finished -> enqueued result idx=1
2026-03-05T12:11:02.014Z merger: write_at_index(1) -> overwrote previous entry
```
alice (QA): So two different tool calls both computed idx=1 and the second overwrote the first.
zack (eng-runtime): That confirms a non-atomic index allocation. I think the fast path increments a shared counter without atomic ops when `parallel_tools=true`. Patch candidate: use unique `tool_call_id` provided by caller, fallback to server-generated UUID, and write by `tool_call_id` map rather than array index.
maya (Support): Customer also reported token billing weirdness — billed tokens match both tool outputs sometimes. Nina, can you check billing hit pattern for cid_07f4e9?
nina (Billing): I looked up cid_07f4e9 and see two token charges roughly same time for the same request_id; that matches double-write symptoms. I'll flag invoice draft and hold charges until fix.
lee (eng-oncall): Action items: 1) zack to prepare a hotfix branch to make merge atomic / map-by-call-id. 2) alice to produce minimal repro harness and attach `x-rw-debug` trace. 3) support to notify customer and put them on the canary fix. 4) billing to hold charges and postmortem after release.
zack (eng-runtime): I'll open PR with tests for concurrent writes and add a canary rollout plan. Tentative patch: use `ConcurrentHashMap<String, ToolResult>` keyed by `tool_call_id` and ensure server generates stable uuid if caller omits.
lee (eng-oncall): Also add temporary log metric `tool_result_missing_call_id` and alert if rate > 1% after deploy.
